display.purpose: Page titles on admin list pages. Once per screen.

body.purpose: All default text, table cells, form labels. Cap 65-75ch in prose.

label.purpose: Filter labels, column headers, small captions. Sentence-case, not uppercase.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Popovers, dropdowns, dialogs. The only structural shadow.

motion.name: crossfade
motion.purpose: Reduced-motion-safe content swaps on POS surface.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary page action (e.g. Add Brand). Operational Navy fill, white text, raised, uppercase label.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #00539b; color: #ffffff; padding: 10px 18px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; font-family: Lato, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0; transition: background 0.2s ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #003d74; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #002d57; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #00539b; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Outlined Button
components.description: Filter toggle and secondary actions. Transparent ground, ink text, outlined. Switches to primary severity when a filter is active.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: transparent; color: #1e293b; padding: 10px 18px; border: 1px solid #334155; border-radius: 6px; font-family: Lato, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px; transition: background 0.2s ease, border-color 0.2s ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #f1f5f9; border-color: #00539b; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #00539b; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Icon Row Action
components.description: Edit / delete / restore actions inside table rows. Text + rounded + large, muted icon. Tactile but restrained.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-icon" aria-label="Edit"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M11 4H4a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v14a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h14a2 2 0 0 0 2-2v-7"/><path d="M18.5 2.5a2.121 2.121 0 0 1 3 3L12 15l-4 1 1-4 9.5-9.5z"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-icon { background: transparent; color: #64748b; padding: 8px; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-icon:hover { background: #f1f5f9; color: #00539b; } .ds-btn-icon:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #00539b; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Search Input
components.description: Canonical list-page search. Leading Font Awesome icon, field fills available width.
components.css: .ds-search { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; width: 320px; } .ds-search-icon { position: absolute; left: 10px; color: #64748b; display: inline-flex; } .ds-search-input { background: #ffffff; color: #1e293b; border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 10px 8px 32px; font-family: Lato, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; width: 100%; transition: border-color 0.2s ease; } .ds-search-input::placeholder { color: #64748b; } .ds-search-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #00539b; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #00539b; }

components.name: Surface Card
components.description: Wraps DataTable on list pages. White (light) / surface-800 (dark), 8px radius, 1px border, 16px padding, no shadow at rest.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px; } .ds-card-body { color: #1e293b; font-family: Lato, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Admin sidebar item. Transparent ground, ink text, 10px 14px padding, 6px radius. Active route uses Instrument 50 background + Trust Blue 700 text.
components.html: Brands
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; background: transparent; color: #1e293b; padding: 10px 14px; border-radius: 6px; text-decoration: none; font-family: Lato, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; transition: background 0.2s ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: #f1f5f9; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: #edf3fa; color: #002d57; } .ds-nav-icon { display: inline-flex; } .ds-nav-label { line-height: 1; }

components.name: Count Tag
components.description: Rounded secondary-severity Tag for counts (e.g. products-per-brand). Small, tonal, never decorative.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: #475569; color: #ffffff; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 2px 10px; font-family: Lato, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; min-width: 24px; height: 20px; }

narrative.overview:
This is the instrument panel of a well-run shop. Each reading is precise, each control has a clear next action, and nothing on screen is decorative. The operator — admin in the back office, sales rep at the counter — should feel they are looking at the truth of the operation, not a presentation about it. Every visual decision answers the question: does this help the next action happen faster, or does it compete with the data?

The system is built on PrimeVue 4 with a custom Aura preset; the library owns component-level styling and this spec does not re-spec what PrimeVue already commits. What this spec owns is the brand layer on top: the custom Operational Navy primary ramp, the surface-token bridge into Tailwind, the two-register divergence between admin density and POS speed, the reduced-motion budget, and the anti-references that keep the tool from drifting toward consumer-app or legacy-POS territory. The login surface is a separate Vue application with its own Noir (zinc-based) theme and is documented here as a named exception, not a second system.
keyCharacteristics: Instrument-grade, not decorative: data and status carry the interface; chrome recedes.
Two registers share tokens, diverge in layout: admin (dense, sidebar) and POS (large hit targets, motion-reduced, tablet-first, 768px floor).
One primary color, used sparingly: Operational Navy #00539b appears on primary actions, active state, and key status — never as background wash or atmosphere.
Light and dark themes are first-class; dark mode via .app-dark dual trigger.
Motion is a budget, not a feature: state transitions only, instant on POS-critical paths, prefers-reduced-motion respected everywhere.

rules.name: The One Instrument Rule
rules.body: Operational Navy appears on primary actions, active state, and key status only — never as atmosphere. If the primary color covers more than ~10% of a screen, the screen is shouting, not designing.

rules.name: The No-Wash Rule
rules.body: Never use Operational Navy (or any primary ramp step) as a full-bleed section background, a gradient, or a decorative tint. The only permitted tinted background is Instrument 50 for the active sidebar route.

rules.name: The Status-Pairs Rule
rules.body: Color is never the sole carrier of state. Every status indicator pairs its color with a label, icon, or shape so it survives color-blindness and grayscale printing.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Lato only. Never introduce a second family for emphasis. Emphasis is weight and size, not a different typeface.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: Do not add tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows above sections. Labels are sentence-case at 14px/500.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces are flat. A shadow on a resting card is a bug, not a design choice. Shadows appear only when an element is elevated above the surface.

rules.name: The Tonal-Layering Rule
rules.body: When you need to separate two surfaces, change the surface token before reaching for a border, and reach for a border before reaching for a shadow.

dos: Do use Operational Navy (#00539b) only for primary actions, active state, and key status — and keep it under ~10% of any screen (The One Instrument Rule).
Do darken on hover/active (#003d74 -> #002d57). Primary controls depress; they never glow or scale.
Do pair every status color with a label or icon. Color confirms; it never carries state alone (The Status-Pairs Rule).
Do separate surfaces by surface token first, border second, shadow last (The Tonal-Layering Rule). Resting cards are flat with a 1px border.
Do keep hit targets large on the POS surface and respect the 768px floor — the POS unsupported-viewport message is a feature, not a fallback.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on every transition; POS-critical paths default to instant or crossfade regardless of the user setting.
Do use Lato in weight and size for hierarchy. One family, multiple weights (The One-Family Rule).
Do use sentence-case 14px/500 for labels. Labels read like labels, not kickers (The No-Kicker Rule).
Do keep body text at >=7:1 (Ink) and muted text at >=4.5:1 (Muted) against surface-card in both themes.
Do import PrimeVue components directly from primevue and use Ziggy's route() for URLs — never hardcode.
donts: Don't use Operational Navy as a full-bleed background, gradient, or decorative tint (The No-Wash Rule). The only tinted background is Instrument 50 on the active sidebar route.
Don't ship a shadow on a resting card (The Flat-By-Default Rule). Shadows are for overlays and dialogs only.
Don't nest cards. A card inside a card is always wrong on this surface.
Don't add a side-stripe border (border-left / border-right > 1px) as a colored accent on cards, list items, or alerts. Use a full border, a background tint, or nothing.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text + gradient). Emphasis is weight or size, in Operational Navy.
Don't add a tiny uppercase tracked eyebrow above every section. The all-caps kicker is the AI scaffold this system rejects (The No-Kicker Rule).
Don't build the hero-metric template (big number, small label, supporting stats, gradient accent) on the dashboard. That is the generic-SaaS anti-reference from PRODUCT.md.
Don't ship the cluttered legacy POS look: tiny fonts, dense unstyled tables, chrome competing with content. The POS is a modern instrument, not a cash-register emulator.
Don't ship over-designed consumer-app flourish: playful animations, large decorative illustrations, gradient hero blobs. This is a tool, not a vibe.
Don't introduce a second typeface for emphasis (The One-Family Rule) or a serif/display sans on the app surface.
Don't mix Noir (login) tokens into the app surface, or Operational Navy into the login surface. The two themes are a deliberate tonal contrast.
Don't use color as the sole carrier of state. A red border without a label fails the audit trail this product exists to provide.
Don't animate layout properties (width, height, padding) where a transform or opacity will do. Motion is a budget, not a feature.
